title: Semrush and performance.io Research Reveals How Pharma Brands Appear in Google AI Overviews
summary: 11/16/26 Semrush and performance.io Research Reveals How Pharma Brands Appear in Google AI Overviews Research from Semrush and performance.io shows that organic rankings remain closely linked to AI visibility, while pharma brands receive a smaller share of citations than their rankings suggest. Semrush, an Adobe company and the leading brand visibility platform, has shared early findings from joint research with specialist pharma and healthcare agency performance.io. The study found that 83.8% of Google AI Overview citations across the pharma searches analyzed came from domains ranking in the organic top 10. When an AI Overview appeared, the domain ranking No. 1 organically was cited 68.8% of the time. Citation rates declined as organic positions fell. The conclusion for pharma marketers: organic rankings remain important in AI search. But rankings alone do not show whether a brand is included in the AI-generated answer. Pharma brands face a gap between rankings and citations Across the sampled queries, pharma brand sites held 9.2% of No. 1 organic rankings but received just 4.2% of AI Overview citations—the largest proportional drop among the domain types tracked. That gap matters because AI Overviews appeared ahead of every other search results feature 98.6% of the time when present. A brand can rank first organically and still be missing from the answer above its link. As agentic search evolves, we’re observing that SEO plays a critical role in how pharma brands are being cited and chosen in AI Search. In our sample, No. 1 ranking came with an AI Overview citation almost seven times in 10. The teams that keep investing in the fundamentals, earning both rank and citations, are the ones that will move through this transition intact -Matt Lowe, CEO of performance.io For pharma marketers, the findings support continuing to invest in SEO while measuring citations alongside rankings and traffic. The practical question is whether a brand’s strong organic position also translates into being cited as a source in AI Overviews. Four years of pharma search data Previewed at Semrush Spotlight 2026, the research was led by performance.io using Semrush Position Tracking data. The study analyzed: 14,300+ keywords , covering branded and non-branded U.S. desktop searches. 689,100+ keyword snapshots across 48 months, from August 2022 to July 2026. Five therapeutic areas: Alzheimer’s disease, type 2 diabetes, non-small-cell lung cancer, plaque psoriasis and respiratory syncytial virus. Working with our agency partners allows us to see what's changing in search before it shows up in industry reports. The team at performance.io brought deep pharma expertise to Semrush data, and the result gives pharma marketers evidence to plan with. - David Power, Global Head of Partnerships at Semrush, an Adobe company The broader white paper also examines healthcare professional and patient searches, buying-signal queries and five brand case studies. About the research The findings describe associations within the sampled U.S. desktop pharma queries, not causation. AI Overview analysis covers September 2024 to July 2026, with citations matched at domain level rather than to individual URLs. The study does not measure clicks or user behavior; traffic figures in the white paper are modelled estimates. Availability Read the research summary: Rank Still Wins: How Organic Position Drives AI Overview Citations in Pharma Search.
body_markdown:
11/16/26


Semrush and performance.io Research Reveals How Pharma Brands Appear in Google AI Overviews


Research from Semrush and performance.io shows that organic rankings remain closely linked to AI visibility, while pharma brands receive a smaller share of citations than their rankings suggest.


Semrush, an Adobe company and the leading brand visibility platform, has shared early findings from joint research with specialist pharma and healthcare agency performance.io. The study found that 83.8% of Google AI Overview citations across the pharma searches analyzed came from domains ranking in the organic top 10.


When an AI Overview appeared, the domain ranking No. 1 organically was cited 68.8% of the time. Citation rates declined as organic positions fell. The conclusion for pharma marketers: organic rankings remain important in AI search. But rankings alone do not show whether a brand is included in the AI-generated answer.


Pharma brands face a gap between rankings and citations


Across the sampled queries, pharma brand sites held 9.2% of No. 1 organic rankings but received just 4.2% of AI Overview citations—the largest proportional drop among the domain types tracked.


That gap matters because AI Overviews appeared ahead of every other search results feature 98.6% of the time when present. A brand can rank first organically and still be missing from the answer above its link.


As agentic search evolves, we’re observing that SEO plays a critical role in how pharma brands are being cited and chosen in AI Search. In our sample, No. 1 ranking came with an AI Overview citation almost seven times in 10. The teams that keep investing in the fundamentals, earning both rank and citations, are the ones that will move through this transition intact
-Matt Lowe, CEO of performance.io


For pharma marketers, the findings support continuing to invest in SEO while measuring citations alongside rankings and traffic. The practical question is whether a brand’s strong organic position also translates into being cited as a source in AI Overviews.


Four years of pharma search data


Previewed at Semrush Spotlight 2026, the research was led by performance.io using Semrush Position Tracking data. The study analyzed:


- **14,300+ keywords** , covering branded and non-branded U.S. desktop searches.
- **689,100+ keyword snapshots** across 48 months, from August 2022 to July 2026.
- **Five therapeutic areas:** Alzheimer’s disease, type 2 diabetes, non-small-cell lung cancer, plaque psoriasis and respiratory syncytial virus.


Working with our agency partners allows us to see what's changing in search before it shows up in industry reports. The team at performance.io brought deep pharma expertise to Semrush data, and the result gives pharma marketers evidence to plan with.
- David Power, Global Head of Partnerships at Semrush, an Adobe company


The broader white paper also examines healthcare professional and patient searches, buying-signal queries and five brand case studies.


About the research


The findings describe associations within the sampled U.S. desktop pharma queries, not causation. AI Overview analysis covers September 2024 to July 2026, with citations matched at domain level rather than to individual URLs. The study does not measure clicks or user behavior; traffic figures in the white paper are modelled estimates.


Availability


Read the research summary: Rank Still Wins: How Organic Position Drives AI Overview Citations in Pharma Search.
